| `keyColor` | none       | `{ l, c, h }` in OKLCH: the base skin's accent                                |
| `theme`    | `"system"` | `"light"`, `"dark"` or `"system"` (follows the device)                        |
| `sound`    | `false`    | Short synthesized sounds on interaction, voiced per skin                      |
| `haptics`  | `true`     | A tap on Android, and the system haptic on iOS 18 Safari, for switches and the like |

Every UISet item and every UI SDK component inside takes the skin, popups included: UI SDK
renders them in place, in the browser's top layer, so they inherit it. Web Components use `<uiset-root skin="ink" theme="light"
sound>` the same way.

## Skins

| Skin        | Look                                                                    | Scheme | Faces to load                   |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------- |
| `base`      | Your shadcn theme, or one built from `keyColor`                         | both   | none (your app's)               |
| `blueprint` | A technical drawing: cyanotype paper, linework, hatching                | dark   | Barlow Semi Condensed           |
| `studio`    | A synth rack: gunmetal panels, rubber pads, amber lamps                 | dark   | Saira Semi Condensed            |
| `phosphor`  | A green-screen terminal: intensity, inverse video, faint scan lines     | dark   | Spline Sans Mono                |
| `ink`       | E-paper: ink on grey, dotted greys, a reading serif, no motion at all   | light  | Literata, Atkinson Hyperlegible |

Each skin falls back to system faces when its own aren't loaded; load them from Google
Fonts or self-host them for the intended look. The themed skins have one scheme, so
`theme` doesn't change them. The design notes for each are in `docs/studio.md`,
`docs/phosphor.md` and `docs/ink.md`.

Every skin is checked in every component and kit, in each scheme it has: text 4.5:1,
control edges and focus 3:1 (axe in the test suite), chart colors told apart with color
blindness (`tests/unit/chart-palette.test.ts`).

## The key color

The base skin builds its accent from one OKLCH color: solid buttons, checked controls,
the selected day, focus rings. Text on it picks black or white by lightness, and dark mode
lifts the ring toward white so it stays visible.

### A whole theme from one color

The [theme generator](https://uiset.dev/themes/generator) goes further than a key
color. From one color, a neutral tint, a radius, a density and a text size, it builds every
token for light and dark: surfaces, text, edges, focus, the four status tones and eight
chart colors. It checks 32 pairs in each scheme (text 4.5:1, controls and focus 3:1, chart
colors 3:1 and apart under color blindness), moves any derived color that fails to the
nearest lightness that passes, and offers a one-click fix when the key itself fails.

It exports the result three ways: a UISet skin file (use it with `skin="custom"`, or the
name you give it), shadcn/ui variables for `:root` and `.dark`, and W3C design tokens. The
address keeps every setting, so a link reopens the same theme.

### With a shadcn/ui theme

With no `keyColor`, the base skin adopts the shadcn theme already on the page:
`--background`, `--foreground`, `--muted`, `--muted-foreground`, `--border`, `--input`,
`--primary` and `--radius`. UISet components then match the rest of your app, and your
theme switcher keeps working.

## Dark mode

`theme="system"` follows the device; `"light"` and `"dark"` pin it for the subtree. The
base skin's colors use `light-dark()`, so a light section inside a dark page is just
another `<UISet theme="light">`.

## Nesting

Skins only set variables, so the nearest root wins. A Blueprint panel inside a Base app:

```tsx
<UISet skin="base">
  <Settings />
  <UISet skin="blueprint">
    <Schematic />
  </UISet>
</UISet>
```

## Your own parts

Style your own markup with the variables, and it follows every skin:

| Variable                                   | What it is                                      |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `--ui-background`, `--ui-foreground`       | The surface and its text                        |
| `--ui-muted`, `--ui-muted-foreground`      | Quiet surfaces, and secondary text (4.5:1)      |
| `--ui-border`, `--ui-input`                | Hairlines, and control edges (3:1)              |
| `--ui-primary`, `--ui-primary-foreground`  | The accent and text on it                       |
| `--ui-ring-border`                         | Focus rings                                     |
| `--ui-radius`, `--ui-font-sans`, `--ui-font-mono` | Corners and faces                         |
| `--tone-info`, `--tone-success`, `--tone-warning`, `--tone-danger` | Status colors, readable as text |
| `--chart-1` … `--chart-8`, `--chart-seq-1` … `--chart-seq-7` | Data colors, in a fixed order     |

## Writing a skin

A skin is a stylesheet in the `uiset.skin` layer that sets variables on its own selector:

```css
@layer ui-sdk, uiset.tokens, uiset.base, uiset.skin;

@layer uiset.skin {
  [data-uiset][data-skin="harbor"] {
    color-scheme: light;
    --ui-background: oklch(0.97 0.01 220);
    --ui-foreground: oklch(0.25 0.03 230);
    --ui-primary: oklch(0.45 0.12 230);
    --ui-primary-foreground: white;
    /* …and the rest of the table above */
  }
}
```

Then `<UISet skin="harbor">`. Keep the contrast rules (text 4.5:1, edges and focus 3:1),
and check it the way UISet's skins are checked: add it to the skin loops in
`tests/e2e/components.spec.ts` and run axe. Decoration a variable can't express (a
texture, a bevel) may use selectors under the same `[data-uiset][data-skin]`, so nested
skins never inherit it.

## Sound and haptics

`sound` turns on short sounds for presses, toggles, selection and errors, made with Web
Audio (no files). Each skin picks a voice (`--uiset-sound`: `soft`, `mechanical`, `beep`
or `paper`); `--uiset-sound-volume` sets the level. Sounds follow UI SDK's own events, so
they play for agents' changes too. Haptics are on by default where the device has them.

## Motion and system settings

UISet's motion stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`; Ink has none at all. In Windows'
forced colors, state that relied on fills becomes borders, and Phosphor drops its bloom
and scan lines.


<!-- docs/migrate-from-shadcn.md -->

# Coming from shadcn/ui

UISet installs with the same CLI into the same folder, and its base skin adopts your
shadcn theme. What changes is underneath: components are UI SDK's, so keyboard, focus,
screen reader and agent behavior come built in, and the API follows UI SDK's.

## Moving an app over

1. **Commit first.** UISet items have the same file names as shadcn's
   (`components/ui/button.tsx`), and the CLI asks before it overwrites one.
2. **Add the root** and wrap the app. Your theme variables are picked up as they are:

   ```bash
   npx shadcn@latest add superzero11/uiset/uiset
   ```

   ```tsx
   <UISet skin="base">
     <App />
   </UISet>
   ```

3. **Replace components one at a time**, starting with leaves (button, badge, input) and
   then the composite ones (dialog, select, menu). Each item is independent, so the app
   keeps working between steps.
4. **Run your tests.** Selectors by role and name keep working; selectors on Radix's
   `data-state` need the UI SDK attributes below.

## What maps to what

| shadcn/ui            | UISet item        | Notes                                                                 |
| -------------------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Button               | `button`          | `variant`: `solid` (default), `outline`, `ghost`                      |
| Input, Label, Form   | `field`           | `Field`, `FieldLabel`, `Input`, `FieldDescription`, `FieldError`; native forms, no form library needed |
| Select               | `select`          | `SelectTrigger` shows the chosen value by itself; `SelectLabel` names it |
| DropdownMenu         | `menu`            | `Menu`, `MenuTrigger`, `MenuContent`, `MenuItem`; handle `onAction` on the menu |
| Dialog               | `dialog`          | `Dialog`, `DialogTrigger`, `DialogContent`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogClose`; no Header or Footer parts, use your own markup |
| AlertDialog          | `alert-dialog`    | Same parts with an `AlertDialog` prefix                               |
| Sheet                | `drawer`          | `Drawer`, with snap points and a handle                               |
| Popover, Tooltip, HoverCard | `popover`, `tooltip`, `hover-card` | Same idea, UI SDK's parts            |
| Tabs                 | `tabs`            | `TabsTab` for TabsTrigger, `TabsPanel` for TabsContent                |
| Accordion            | `accordion`       | `AccordionItem`, `AccordionTrigger`, `AccordionPanel` for AccordionContent |
| Command              | `command`         | `CommandInput`, `CommandList`, `CommandItem`, `CommandEmpty`          |
| Toast (Sonner)       | `toast`           | `toast("Saved", { description })`, with a `ToastRegion` in the app    |
| Checkbox, Switch, Slider, RadioGroup | `checkbox`, `switch`, `slider`, `radio` | Same use; Slider takes a number or an array |
| Calendar, DatePicker | `calendar`, `date-picker` | Plus `date-input` and `time-input` for typed dates            |
| Table, DataTable     | `data-grid`       | Sorting, filters, grouping, pinning, editing and virtual rows built in |
| Card, Badge, Alert, Skeleton, Breadcrumb | `card`, `badge`, `alert`, `skeleton`, `breadcrumbs` | See [App frame and data display](./app-shell.md) |
| Sidebar              | `app-shell`       | A sidebar that collapses to icons and becomes a drawer on phones      |
| Chart (Recharts)     | `line-chart`, `bar-chart`, … | No chart library: keyboard-explorable, with a table view    |

Things shadcn/ui doesn't have: the [chat kit](./chat.md), a
[rich text editor](./rich-text.md), [board](./board.md), [scheduler](./scheduler.md),
[canvas](./canvas.md), [IDE](./ide.md), [terminal](./terminal.md), the
[Agent Console](./agent-console.md) and whole-page [templates](./templates.md).

## API differences

- **`asChild` becomes `render`.** `<Button asChild><a href="/">Home</a></Button>` is
  `<Button render={<a href="/" />}>Home</Button>`.
- **State attributes.** Radix's `data-state="open"` and `data-state="checked"` are
  `data-open` and `data-checked` (also `data-pressed`, `data-highlighted`,
  `data-disabled`). Every part has a `data-slot`, like `data-slot="dialog-content"`.
- **Change handlers** are `onValueChange`, `onOpenChange`, `onCheckedChange` and
  `onPressedChange`, with a second `details` argument that says why it changed (a click,
  a key, an agent) and can cancel it.
- **Styling.** UISet ships plain CSS in cascade layers, not Tailwind classes. Tailwind
  keeps working beside it: put a class on any part, and since your utilities aren't in
  UISet's layers, they win.
- **Names for agents.** UI SDK's agent bridge finds controls by their accessible names.
  A control with a visible label is already named; an icon button needs `aria-label`.

## Theme

Nothing to change: the base skin reads `--background`, `--foreground`, `--muted`,
`--muted-foreground`, `--border`, `--input`, `--primary` and `--radius`. To set the
accent without a shadcn theme, pass `keyColor`, or try one in the
[theme generator](https://uiset.dev/themes/generator), which also exports shadcn/ui variables. See [Theming](./theming.md).


<!-- docs/roadmap.md -->

# Roadmap

UISet grows with UI SDK. This page says what's done, what's next, and what we won't do.

## Shipped

- **The root and five skins**: Base (adopts your shadcn theme, or one key color),
  Blueprint, Studio, Phosphor and Ink, with sound and haptics.
- **All 55 UI SDK components**, styled, each its own item; and 16 app frame and data
  display parts.
- **Twelve kits**: chat, rich text, data grid, charts, board, scheduler, canvas, IDE,
  mobile, terminal, Studio and the Agent Console.
- **Ten page templates**: auth, dashboard, settings, admin, inbox, chat app, project board,
  calendar, pricing and IDE.
- **Web Components**: every kit and template as custom elements.
- **For coding agents**: skills, llms.txt and Markdown docs.
- **The theme generator**: one color in, a complete, checked theme out.

## Next

- **More skins.** Cockpit (guarded switches, gauges), Paper (cards, tape, corkboard) and
  Print (brutalist type), each with its own sound.
- **Framework guides.** Step-by-step setups for Vue, Svelte, Solid and Angular with the Web
  Components build.
- **More templates.** Onboarding, an agent-wired settings console, and a docs site.
- **Listing.** The shadcn registry directory, so items install as `@uiset/<item>`.

## Following UI SDK

UI SDK is in public beta. UISet pins its exact version and moves with each release after
the full test suite passes in every skin. Problems we find in UI SDK go upstream as issues,
with a test that shows them.

## What we won't do

- Copy the look of a real product or brand. Every skin is an original design.
- Put a second UI library underneath. Behavior always comes from UI SDK.
- Use "Vercel" in a product name. UISet is a community project, not affiliated with Vercel.

## Asking for things

Open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/superzero11/uiset/issues) with what you're
building and what's missing. Kits and templates that many people need come first.


<!-- docs/blueprint.md -->

# Blueprint

A technical drawing: cyanotype paper, white linework, hatching for filled states,
dimension lines for slider tracks, and lettering for labels. It was the first themed skin,
built to prove that a skin can change everything about how UI SDK's components look while
changing nothing about how they behave.

```tsx
<UISet skin="blueprint">…</UISet>
```

## Tokens

| Name   | Value                         | Role                                                   |
| ------ | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Paper  | `oklch(0.36 0.11 254)`        | The page: a deep cyanotype blue                        |
| Line   | `oklch(0.96 0.02 230)`        | Text, borders, fills: drawn in white                   |
| Faint  | Line at 16%                   | Hover fills and the fine grid                          |
| Grid   | Line at 7%                    | The 8px and 64px drawing grid on the paper             |
| Ring   | `oklch(0.9 0.13 200)`         | Focus: a cyan line, distinct from the white drawing    |

**Type.** Barlow Semi Condensed; labels and buttons in spaced capitals, like drafting
lettering.

**Drawing language.**

- Text boxes are a line to write on, not a box.
- Checked and filled states are hatched, not filled solid: a switch's track, a slider's
  range.
- Slider tracks are dimension lines with end ticks; the thumb is a diamond.
- Popups are a sheet laid on the drawing, with an offset shadow line.
- What isn't reached yet (an empty star, an upcoming step) is drawn faint.

**Scheme.** Dark only: `theme` doesn't change it.

**Contrast.** White linework on the paper clears 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for every control
edge; the chart colors are a set chosen for the blue paper and checked for color blindness
(neighbors CVD ΔE ≥ 14.6).


<!-- docs/studio.md -->

# Studio: design plan

**Subject.** A rack of synthesizer modules on a studio desk: painted metal faceplates,
rubber knob caps, silk-screened legends, amber indicator lamps and patch cables.
**Audience.** Developers building music, audio and creative tools, and anyone who wants
an interface that feels like hardware. **Job.** The demo that makes the skin system
obvious: the same UI SDK components, turned into instruments you can hear.

Not SPEC-01 (light molded pocket instruments, LCDs, orange-red keys). Studio is darker,
rack-mounted, metal and rubber, with color reserved for cables and lamps.

## Tokens

| Name   | Value                           | Role                                    |
| ------ | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Rack   | `oklch(0.25 0.01 255)`          | Rails and the gaps between modules      |
| Panel  | `oklch(0.34 0.012 255)`         | Module faceplates (gunmetal, not black) |
| Legend | `oklch(0.94 0.012 85)`          | Silk-screened text and scales           |
| Rubber | `oklch(0.19 0.006 255)`         | Knob caps, pads                         |
| Lamp   | `oklch(0.82 0.15 72)`           | The key color: lit state, value arcs    |
| Cables | red, blue, green, amber, violet | Which cable is which                    |

**Type.** Saira Semi Condensed. Legends are small and uppercase because that is how
faceplates are printed; readouts use tabular numerals. Body copy stays sentence case.

**Layout.** Modules sit side by side on a rack, each with screws at the corners and its
name at the top. Controls on a grid, jacks along the bottom, cables drape over all of it.

**Principles.**

1. Spend boldness on the cables and the lamps. Panels stay quiet.
2. Every state a person sets lights something: a switch lamp, a step, a knob arc.
3. Depth is a 1px top highlight and a bottom shadow, never a blur haze. Forced colors
   replaces all of it with borders.
4. Sound is mechanical: thocks for pads, detent clicks for knobs, latches for switches.

**Review against generic defaults.** Dark UI with one accent is a common default; here
the panel is mid-dark gunmetal, the lamp color comes from real indicator lamps, and the
five cable colors carry meaning. Uppercase is limited to printed legends.


<!-- docs/phosphor.md -->

# Phosphor: design plan

**Subject.** A monochrome video terminal on a lab bench: a curved glass tube with green
phosphor glyphs, a faint bloom around bright text, scan lines you only notice up close,
a block cursor, and boxes drawn with line characters. **Audience.** Developers building
developer tools: CLIs in the browser, infrastructure consoles, logs, agents, and anyone
who wants their app to feel like a terminal. **Job.** The skin that makes developers
share a screenshot, and the natural partner of the Terminal kit.

Named Phosphor, not Terminal, so the skin never gets confused with the Terminal kit.

## Tokens

| Name    | Value                     | Role                                                      |
| ------- | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tube    | `oklch(0.26 0.035 155)`   | The glass: a dark green-grey, never black                 |
| Raster  | `oklch(0.3 0.04 155)`     | Raised surfaces (popups, cards): a brighter scan area     |
| Dim     | `oklch(0.75 0.11 150)`    | Half-intensity text: secondary text, borders, placeholders |
| Glow    | `oklch(0.88 0.17 148)`    | Full-intensity text and the key color                     |
| Inverse | Glow fill, Tube text      | Selection, the chosen item, solid buttons                 |
| Signals | P3 amber `oklch(0.84 0.15 75)`, P22 red `oklch(0.75 0.16 28)`, P4 white `oklch(0.95 0.02 150)`, P7 blue `oklch(0.8 0.1 230)` | Data series and status, each a real phosphor type |

**Type.** One monospace for everything, because a terminal has one character grid:
"Spline Sans Mono", falling back to the platform's monospace. Body 14px with 1.5 line
height; headings are the same face at a heavier weight, never uppercase.

**Layout.** Everything aligns to the character grid: 0 radius, 1px Dim borders as if
drawn with box characters, spacing in multiples of half a line. Popups are a brighter
raster area with a Glow border, no shadow.

**Principles.**

1. The interface is monochrome. Color is intensity: Dim, Glow, and Inverse video. Only
   data and status use the other phosphors, so they stand out.
2. A chosen thing is drawn in inverse video: the selected day, the active tab, the
   checked switch track, the highlighted menu item, solid buttons.
3. Bright text blooms a little (a tight text-shadow on Glow text only). Scan lines are a
   static, very faint pattern on the background, never on text, and never animated; no
   flicker, no blinking except the text caret.
4. Focus is a 2px Glow outline offset by 2px, unmissable on the dark tube.
5. Sound is the `beep` voice: short square-wave chirps.
6. Forced colors drops bloom and scan lines; reduced transparency drops scan lines.

**Contrast** (computed). Glow on Tube 11.4:1, Dim on Tube 7.2:1, Tube on Glow (inverse)
11.4:1. Dim started at L 0.68 (5.6:1 on the tube); axe found it under 4.5:1 on tinted
surfaces (badges, avatar chips, event blocks), so it went up to L 0.75, which clears 4.5:1
on all of them; red went from 0.72 to 0.75 for the danger badge. Borders in Dim clear 3:1.

**Charts** (validated, `tests/unit/chart-palette.test.ts`): the tube's green, then blue,
P3 amber, P22 red, P4 white, lavender, cyan and pink, each 3:1 or more on the tube;
neighbors CVD ΔE ≥ 9.5 and normal ≥ 17, the first six pairwise CVD ≥ 9.4.

**As shipped.** Inside inverse video, quiet text and chips reverse too (a menu item's
hint, a tab's count). Code uses white for keywords, amber for strings and constants, blue
for functions, Dim for comments; the Terminal kit's ANSI colors are the phosphors.

**Review against generic defaults.** "Near-black with one acid-green accent" is a known
default. Phosphor differs on purpose: the background is a green-grey glass, not near
black; green is not an accent on neutral UI but the only ink, in intensity steps; the
signature is inverse video for selection, which defaults don't do; and the second colors
are named phosphors used only for data. Monospace here is the subject's own type, used
for everything rather than for small labels.


<!-- docs/ink.md -->

# Ink: design plan

**Subject.** An electronic-paper reader: a matte, light grey screen, crisp black type,
greys made of fine dots, and pages that change by redrawing rather than animating.
**Audience.** Reading and writing apps, documentation, note-taking and focus tools, and
products that want the calmest, highest-contrast interface with no motion at all.
**Job.** The first light themed skin, and proof that the system works with no color.

Named Ink, after the medium, rather than any e-reader brand.

## Tokens

| Name   | Value                  | Role                                                        |
| ------ | ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| Screen | `oklch(0.95 0 0)`      | The paper: a neutral light grey, not white and not cream    |
| Ink    | `oklch(0.2 0 0)`       | Text, borders, solid fills: the only "color"                |
| Grey   | `oklch(0.42 0 0)`      | Secondary text (7.3:1 on Screen)                            |
| Tint   | `oklch(0.88 0 0)`      | Quiet fills: hover, muted surfaces, tracks                  |
| Dots   | a 2px dot screen of Ink on Screen | Mid-grey fills (progress, chart series, range middles) drawn as dither, the way the medium does it |
| Hatch  | 45° lines of Ink       | A second fill texture, for danger and for a second data series |

**Type.** Two faces with distinct jobs. "Literata", a typeface designed for reading on
screens, for headings and long text; "Atkinson Hyperlegible", designed for legibility,
for controls, labels and data. Body 16px; serif text gets 1.6 line height, controls 1.4.

**Layout.** Calm and flat: 1.5px Ink borders on controls, 6px radius, generous padding,
no shadows. Popups are Screen with a 2px Ink border, so they read as a sheet laid on top.

**Principles.**

1. No color, so meaning never depends on it. Status pairs an icon and a word with a fill
   pattern: solid for success, dots for warning, hatch for danger.
2. No motion. Every transition and animation duration is zero, whatever the person's
   motion setting; a change is a redraw.
3. Chosen things are solid Ink with Screen text: the selected day, checked boxes, the
   active segment, solid buttons. Hover is the Tint fill.
4. Focus is a 3px Ink outline offset by 2px.
5. Sound is the `paper` voice, quiet; haptics stay on where the device has them.
6. Forced colors maps straight across, since the skin already avoids color.

**Contrast** (computed). Ink on Screen 15.6:1, Grey on Screen 7.3:1 and on Tint 5.9:1,
Screen on Ink (inverse) 15.6:1; Ink borders clear 3:1 easily.

**Review against generic defaults.** A light skin with a serif risks the "cream paper,
serif display, terracotta accent" default. Ink avoids each part: the screen is a neutral
grey, not warm; there is no accent color at all; the serif is a reading face used for
reading, paired with a legibility face for controls; and greys are dot screens rather
than flat tints. It's flat but not broadsheet: radius stays 6px and there are no
hairline column rules.

**As shipped** (2026-11-15).

- **Data is the one exception to "no color."** The plan drew chart series as dots and
  hatching, but the chart kit fills marks with a color per series and has no patterns, so
  a legend could not show which pattern is which. Charts and calendar events take a muted,
  print-like set instead, like a color e-paper panel: ink, blue, orange, sage, dark red,
  purple, teal, mustard, each 3:1 or more on the screen; neighbors CVD ΔE ≥ 9.8 and
  normal ≥ 16, the first six pairwise (`tests/unit/chart-palette.test.ts`). The interface
  itself stays ink only.
- Body text is 15px (0.9375rem), not 16px: at 16px the denser kits (data grid, IDE,
  scheduler) cramped. Rich text and chat answers get the 1.6 line height.
- Status: solid bars for information and success, dots for warnings, hatching for danger,
  each with its icon and word. A destructive button is framed in a double rule; an invalid
  field has a dashed edge.
- An empty rating star is a screen of dots; a loading skeleton is dots, not a shimmer.
- Code is set in ink and grey. Inside a solid (selected) row, quiet text reverses to a
  light grey.
- No motion is set inside the skin, so it holds whatever the motion setting.



<!-- docs/app-shell.md -->

# App frame and data display

The frame an app's pages sit in, and the small parts most pages show. `AppShell` is a
sidebar layout that collapses to icons with Mod+B, remembers that, and moves into a drawer
on narrow screens. Around it are a page header, breadcrumbs, cards, badges, figures, lists,
alerts, loading states, a stepper, a search field and a copy button. Most are plain HTML in
UISet's styles; the ones with behavior use UI SDK: Drawer, Tooltip, Preferences and
shortcuts for the shell, Input for search, and `announce` for copy.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add superzero11/uiset/app-shell superzero11/uiset/breadcrumbs \
  superzero11/uiset/page-header superzero11/uiset/card superzero11/uiset/badge \
  superzero11/uiset/stat superzero11/uiset/empty-state superzero11/uiset/skeleton \
  superzero11/uiset/description-list superzero11/uiset/item-list superzero11/uiset/alert \
  superzero11/uiset/kbd superzero11/uiset/spinner superzero11/uiset/stepper \
  superzero11/uiset/search-field superzero11/uiset/copy-button
```

Each is its own item, so add only the ones you use. They share `shell/shell.css`, and the
ones with icons bring `shell/icons.tsx`.

## Parts

| Part                                                  | Item               | What it is                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AppShell`                                            | `app-shell`        | Sidebar, header and content; icons only with Mod+B; a drawer on narrow screens |
| `SidebarNav`, `SidebarGroup`, `SidebarItem`           | `app-shell`        | The sidebar's links, in titled groups, with icons and badges    |
| `Breadcrumbs`                                         | `breadcrumbs`      | Where you are, the last item marked as the current page        |
| `PageHeader`                                          | `page-header`      | The page's heading, a description and actions                  |
| `Card` and its header, title, description, content and footer | `card`     | A bordered block                                                |
| `Badge`                                               | `badge`            | A short status label in five tones                             |
| `Stat`                                                | `stat`             | A figure with its change in words and color, and an optional trend |
| `EmptyState`                                          | `empty-state`      | What to do when there's nothing here yet                       |
| `Skeleton`, `SkeletonText`, `Loading`                 | `skeleton`         | Placeholder shapes, and a region that says "Loading…" once     |
| `DescriptionList`                                     | `description-list` | Terms and their details                                        |
| `ItemList`, `Item`                                    | `item-list`        | Rows with media, a title, a description, meta and actions      |
| `Alert`                                               | `alert`            | An inline message in four tones that names its tone            |
| `Kbd`                                                 | `kbd`              | Keys the way this platform writes them: ⌘K or Ctrl+K           |
| `Spinner`                                             | `spinner`          | A loading indicator that says what's loading                   |
| `Stepper`                                             | `stepper`          | The steps of a flow, the current one marked, later ones locked |
| `SearchField`                                         | `search-field`     | A search box with Clear and a key that focuses it from anywhere |
| `CopyButton`                                          | `copy-button`      | Copies a value, then says Copied                               |

## Use

```tsx
import { Icon } from "@/components/ui/shell/icons"

<AppShell
  brand={<a href="/">Acme</a>}
  sidebar={
    <SidebarNav label="Main">
      <SidebarGroup title="Workspace">
        <SidebarItem href="/" icon={<Icon name="home" />} current>Overview</SidebarItem>
        <SidebarItem href="/deploys" icon={<Icon name="branch" />}>Deployments</SidebarItem>
      </SidebarGroup>
    </SidebarNav>
  }
  header={<SearchField label="Search projects" placeholder="Search…" />}
>
  <PageHeader
    above={<Breadcrumbs items={[{ label: "Projects", href: "/" }, { label: "Atlas" }]} />}
    title="Atlas"
    description="Production, Europe. Last deployed 4 minutes ago."
    actions={<Button>Deploy</Button>}
  />
  <Stat
    label="Errors"
    value="0.4%"
    change={{ value: "0.1%", direction: "up", good: false, period: "vs last week" }}
    trend={[0.2, 0.3, 0.3, 0.4]}
  />
  {deploys.length === 0 && (
    <EmptyState
      title="No deployments yet"
      description="Push to your main branch and the first one shows up here."
      actions={<Button>Connect a repository</Button>}
    />
  )}
</AppShell>
```

### The shell

- `sidebar` is required; `brand` sits above it and `header` across the top. `children` go
  in a `<main>`; pass `contentElement="div"` when your page already has one.
- `label` ("Navigation") names the sidebar, and titles the drawer when there's no `brand`.
- When the viewport is `narrowBelow` ("48rem") wide or less, the sidebar moves into a
  drawer opened by Open navigation in the header. On the server the shell renders the
  wide layout.
- Expanded or collapsed is saved in `localStorage` under `uiset-sidebar` with UI SDK's
  preferences, and shown as `data-sidebar` on a wrapper. Every shell on the same origin
  shares it, the web element included.
- `SidebarItem` takes `href`, `icon`, `current` (`aria-current="page"`), `badge` and its
  label as text. While the sidebar shows icons only, each link has a tooltip with its
  label. `SidebarGroup`'s `title` names its list; `SidebarNav`'s `label` defaults to
  "Sections".
- `--app-shell-height` (100dvh) sets the shell's height and `--app-shell-pad` the
  content's padding, so a full-bleed page can set it to 0.
- `Icon` takes a `name` from `shell/icon-paths.ts`: `home`, `users`, `orders`, `reports`,
  `settings`, `mail`, `inbox`, `folder`, `file`, `branch`, `star`, `bell` and more.

### Page parts

- `Breadcrumbs` takes `items` (`{ label, href? }`) and `label` ("Breadcrumb"). The last
  item is the current page (`aria-current="page"`) and is never a link.
- `PageHeader` takes `title`, `description`, `actions`, `above` (breadcrumbs, say) and
  `level`: 1 for an `h1` (the default) or 2.
- `Card`, `CardHeader`, `CardDescription`, `CardContent` and `CardFooter` take a `div`'s
  props (a `p`'s for the description). `CardTitle` takes `level` (2, 3 or 4; `h3` by
  default), `className` and `children` only.
- `EmptyState` takes `title`, `description`, `actions`, `icon` (a shell icon name,
  `inbox` by default, or `null`) and `level` (2, 3 or 4; `h2` by default).
- `Stepper` takes `steps` (`{ value, label, description? }`), `value`, `onValueChange`,
  `label` ("Progress") and `linear` (on). Steps before the current one show a check and
  read "(done)"; the current one has `aria-current="step"`; with `linear`, later steps
  are disabled. A `value` that isn't in `steps` marks the first one. The stepper doesn't
  move by itself: your Back and Continue set `value`.

### Data display

- `Badge` takes `tone` (`neutral` by default, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`) and
  a `span`'s props. The tone is color only, so the words you pass carry the meaning.
- `Stat` takes `label`, `value` and `description`. `change` is `{ value, direction, good?,
  period? }`: an arrow plus "Up" or "Down" for screen readers. A rise shows as good and a
  fall as bad; `good` overrides that (`good: false` for errors going up). `trend` (numbers
  oldest first, `null` for a gap) draws a sparkline named for where the values went
  ("Errors trend: from 0.2 to 0.4, low 0.2, high 0.4"), and `format` formats them.
- `DescriptionList` takes `items` (`{ term, details }`) and `layout`: `"columns"` (the
  default) or `"stacked"`.
- `ItemList` takes a `label`, which names the list. Each `Item` takes `title` (a link with
  `href`), `media`, `description`, `meta` and `actions`.
- `Alert` takes `tone` (`info` by default, `success`, `warning`, `danger`), `title`, its
  text as children, `actions` and `onDismiss`, which adds Dismiss. Screen readers hear the
  tone before the title ("Warning: Card expires soon"); an alert with no `title` doesn't
  say it.
- An `Alert` is static by default. `live` makes it a polite `role="status"`; `urgent`
  makes it `role="alert"`, for a message that appears in response to something and must
  interrupt.
- `Kbd` takes `keys` in UI SDK's shortcut form (`"mod+k"`) and shows ⌘K on Apple devices
  and Ctrl+K elsewhere.
- `Spinner` takes `label` ("Loading"), read by screen readers as a status, and `size`
  ("1rem").
- `Skeleton` takes `width`, `height` ("1rem") and `radius`; `SkeletonText` takes `lines`
  (3), the last one shorter. Both are hidden from screen readers. Wrap what's loading in
  `Loading` (`loading`, `label` "Loading…"): it's `aria-busy` while loading and says the
  label once. With reduced motion, skeletons and spinners stop moving.
- `SearchField` takes UI SDK Input's props (`value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`,
  `placeholder`, `name`) plus `label` ("Search") and `shortcut` ("/", or `null` for none).
  The key shows as a hint until there's text; then Clear empties the field and keeps
  focus there.
- `CopyButton` takes `value`, `label` ("Copy") and `copiedLabel` ("Copied"). It writes
  `value` to the clipboard, announces `copiedLabel`, and shows it with a check for 1.6
  seconds. If the clipboard refuses, nothing changes on screen.

## Keys

| Keys                     | Where        | Does                                                       |
| ------------------------ | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mod+B                    | anywhere     | Collapse the sidebar to icons, or expand it (wide screens only) |
| "/" (the `shortcut`)     | anywhere     | Focus the search field, except while typing in another field |
| Escape                   | drawer       | Close the navigation drawer                                |
| Tab, Enter, Space        | stepper      | Each step is a button; locked steps are skipped            |

The sidebar toggle and the search field carry `aria-keyshortcuts` for their keys.

## For agents

Most of these parts are plain HTML, so the bridge doesn't list them: Breadcrumbs,
PageHeader, Card, Badge, Stat, EmptyState, Skeleton, Loading, DescriptionList, ItemList,
Kbd and Spinner. The buttons, links and fields you put in them are listed, by their own
names. Inside an `Item`, a control carries the row's text ("Ada Lovelace ada@acme.dev
Owner"), so when two rows each have a Remove button, the bridge's error lists both with
their rows and the agent picks one by ref.

- **Shell:** the toggle is a button named "Collapse sidebar" or "Expand sidebar". On a
  narrow screen the drawer is "Open navigation", with `setOpen`. Each `SidebarItem` is a
  tooltip named by its link text, with `press` (follows the link) and `setOpen`. A
  `badge`'s text runs into that name with no space ("Deployments3").
- **SearchField:** one input named by `label`, with `setValue` and `clear`. Its Clear
  button is `data-agent-hidden`, so agents don't see a second control.
- **Stepper:** each step is a button named by its text, "Account (done)" for a done step.
  A description runs into the label ("DetailsName and region"). Locked steps are
  disabled and have no actions.
- **CopyButton:** a button named by its text, which reads `copiedLabel` for 1.6 seconds
  after a press.
- **Alert:** Dismiss is a button named "Dismiss"; with two dismissible alerts on a page, a
  step needs the ref.

None of these parts asks for confirmation. Put `data-agent-confirm` on destructive
actions you pass in, as on a Delete in a page header.

## Web Components

`<uiset-app-shell>`, `<uiset-page-header>` and `<uiset-empty-state>` are in
[App Shell](./web-components.md#app-shell). `<uiset-search-field>`, `<uiset-copy-button>`
and `<uiset-stepper>` are in [React and the web](./web-components.md#react-and-the-web)
(there, `shortcut=""` turns the key off), and `<uiset-stat>` is with
[Charts](./web-components.md#charts). Badge, alert, card, item and description lists,
breadcrumbs, skeleton, spinner and kbd are classes in `uiset.css`.


<!-- docs/rich-text.md -->

# Rich text

A rich text editor on UI SDK: headings, lists (nested, numbered, to-dos), quotes, code,
links, mentions, dividers and images, with a toolbar, Markdown as you type, "/" for blocks
and "@" for people. Its value is a small document you can save as Markdown or clean HTML,
and agents read and write it as Markdown through UI SDK's bridge.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add superzero11/uiset/rich-text
```

It has no editor library underneath. The toolbar is UI SDK's Toolbar, Toggles, Select and
Popover; "/" and "@" are UI SDK's TriggerMenu, connected through an editor adapter; undo
is UI SDK's `createUndoStack`. The editing itself (`rich-text/view.ts`, `model.ts`) is
shared by React and Web Components.

## Parts

| Part               | What it is                                                                 |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RichTextEditor`   | The editor: toolbar, text, "/" and "@" menus, an optional count, a form value |
| `RichTextContent`  | Saved text, read-only, in the editor's styles (rendered as React, never as an HTML string) |
| `toMarkdown`, `fromMarkdown`, `toHTML`, `fromHTML`, `toText` | The document to and from Markdown, HTML and plain text |
| `richTextCommands` | What "/" offers by default, to extend or reorder                           |

## Use

```tsx
const [doc, setDoc] = useState(() => fromMarkdown(saved))

<RichTextEditor
  label="Release notes"
  value={doc}
  onValueChange={setDoc}
  placeholder="Write the release notes…"
  mentions={[{ value: "ada", label: "Ada Lovelace" }]}
  maxLength={2000}
/>

// Later: save it.
await save({ markdown: toMarkdown(doc), html: toHTML(doc) })
```

- `defaultValue` takes Markdown or a document, for an editor you don't control. `value`
  takes a document; pass back what `onValueChange` gives you (it fires for edits, not for
  caret moves).
- In a form, `name="notes"` adds a hidden field with the HTML (or Markdown, with
  `format="markdown"`).
- `maxLength` shows a count. Going over is allowed and says so in words ("12 over the limit
  of 2000 characters"), so nothing typed is lost; the field is described by the count.
- `commands` replaces what "/" offers: `{ value, label, description?, icon? | glyph?,
  run(state) }`, where `run` returns the next editor state (`setBlock`, `insertBlock` and
  the rest of `rich-text/model` are there for it). `commands={[]}` turns "/" off.
- `uploadImage(file)` takes pasted, dropped and chosen images; return `{ src, alt? }` or
  `null`. Without it, the toolbar has no image button and image files aren't taken.
- `readOnly` hides the toolbar and refuses edits from people and agents; `disabled` also
  dims it.
- `messages` changes what's announced (marks and blocks turning on and off), for other
  languages.
- `onSubmit` runs on Mod+Enter outside a to-do, for a comment box that sends.

## Safety

Everything that comes in is checked the same way typing is: pasted HTML and Markdown, the
editor's own clipboard format (any page can put it on the clipboard), a `value` or
`defaultValue` document, and what `RichTextContent` shows. Unknown block types become
paragraphs, heading levels and list depths are clamped, and links and images that aren't
`http(s)`, `mailto:`, `tel:` or a path (not `//host`) are dropped, also when a link is
added at a caret with nothing selected. `sanitizeDoc` from `rich-text/model` does it for
your own code.

## The document

A flat list of blocks, each `{ id, type, content }`: `paragraph`, `heading` (`level` 1–3),
`quote`, `code` (`language`), `bullet`, `ordered`, `task` (`checked`) with `indent` 0–4,
`divider` and `image` (`src`, `alt`). `content` is text runs with `marks` (`bold`,
`italic`, `underline`, `strike`, `code`, `link`) and mentions (`{ type: "mention", id,
label }`). It's plain JSON: store it as is, or store Markdown or HTML and read it back.

- **Markdown out** is GitHub-flavored: `- [ ]` tasks, fenced code, `~~strike~~`, nested
  lists by two spaces. Underline has no Markdown; it's kept in HTML only.
- **HTML out** is a small, fixed set of tags (`p`, `h1`–`h3`, `ul`/`ol`/`li`, `blockquote`,
  `pre`/`code`, `strong`, `em`, `u`, `s`, `a`, `hr`, `img`, `br`), with tasks as
  `<li data-checked>`. Text is escaped; links are `http(s)`, `mailto:`, `tel:` or a path.
- **Mentions** are `<span data-mention="id">@Name</span>` in HTML and read back as
  mentions; Markdown has no mention syntax, so there they're plain `@Name` text. Store the
  document or HTML to keep them.
- **HTML in** (paste, `fromHTML`) keeps only what the editor can show. A table's rows
  become lines with their cells apart by tabs. Images in pasted pages come in only when
  you pass `uploadImage` (no hotlinks or tracking pixels otherwise). Scripts, styles,
  event attributes, `javascript:` links and unsafe images are dropped. Bold, italics and
  strikethrough set by Google Docs' and Word's inline styles are read as marks.

## Keys

| Keys                       | Does                                                  |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| Mod+B, Mod+I, Mod+U        | Bold, italic, underline (on the selection, or for what you type next) |
| Mod+Shift+X, Mod+E         | Strikethrough, inline code                            |
| Mod+K                      | Add, edit or remove the link at the selection         |
| Mod+Alt+0, 1, 2, 3         | Text, Heading 1, 2, 3                                 |
| Mod+Shift+7, 8, 9          | Numbered, bulleted, to-do list                        |
| Tab, Shift+Tab             | In a list: nest the item one level deeper, or less    |
| Enter                      | New block; on an empty item, out one level, then out of the list; twice at the end of a code block, out of the code |
| Shift+Enter                | A line break in the same block                        |
| Mod+Enter                  | Check a to-do off, or `onSubmit` elsewhere             |
| Mod+Z, Mod+Shift+Z         | Undo, redo (typing is grouped; an agent's edit is one step) |
| "/" at the start of a line | The block menu: arrows, Enter or Tab, Escape          |
| "@"                        | Mention someone from `mentions`                       |

Markdown as you type: `#`, `##`, `###`, `-`, `1.`, `[ ]`, `[x]`, `>` and a space at the
start of a line; `---` or three backticks then Enter; `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `` `code` ``
and `~~strike~~` as you close them. Pasting Markdown text turns it into blocks.

A to-do's box is a checkbox named by its task; a click or a screen reader's activation
checks it off. Each block takes its own text direction (`dir="auto"`), so Arabic or Hebrew
reads right in a left-to-right app. A read-only editor stays in the Tab order so its text
can be read and copied. Text from an input method takes the marks typing would there.

The toolbar is one Tab stop; arrows move along it. Pressing a button keeps the selection
and puts focus back in the text. Marks and blocks turning on and off are announced.

## For agents

The editor is one component, named by its `label`, with its value as Markdown.
`setValue(markdown)` replaces the text (unchanged Markdown changes nothing),
`insert(markdown)` adds blocks at the end without re-reading what's there, so mentions and
line breaks inside items survive, and `clear()` empties it. Each is one undo step for the person, and read-only or disabled
editors refuse them with a reason. The toolbar is hidden from agents (it acts on a
person's selection); agents format through Markdown instead.

## Web Components

`<uiset-rich-text>` is the same editor, built from UI SDK's own elements. See
[Web Components](./web-components.md#rich-text).


<!-- docs/chat.md -->

# Chat

A chat interface on UI SDK, in five items: the thread and its messages, Markdown answers
that stream, the parts around an answer (reasoning, tool calls, sources), the message box,
and the list of chats. Every part takes plain props, so your model's stream goes into your
own state and the kit draws it. The `chat-app` template puts them together into a page.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add superzero11/uiset/chat superzero11/uiset/chat-response \
  superzero11/uiset/chat-parts superzero11/uiset/chat-composer superzero11/uiset/chat-sidebar
```

Each of the last four brings `chat` with it. `chat-response` also adds `react-markdown`,
`remark-gfm`, `remend` and `shiki`.

The behavior is UI SDK's. The thread follows new text with `createStickToBottom`; the
message box brings back what you sent with `createInputHistory`; "/" and "@" are
`TriggerMenu`; attachments are `FileInput`; reasoning, tool calls and sources are
`Collapsible`; the model picker is a `Select`; usage is a `Meter`.

## Parts

| Part                                  | Item            | What it is                                                     |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ChatThread`                          | `chat`          | The scrolling log: follows new text unless you scroll up, then offers Jump to latest |
| `ChatMessage`                         | `chat`          | One message: who sent it, when, its content and an `actions` slot |
| `ChatMessageActions`                  | `chat`          | Copy, Retry, Edit and Good or Bad under a message, as one toolbar |
| `ChatBranch`                          | `chat`          | "2 of 3" with Previous and Next version, for regenerated answers |
| `ChatEmpty`, `ChatSuggestions`        | `chat`          | The empty thread's heading, and prompts to start from          |
| `ChatTasks`                           | `chat`          | A plan: each task's status in words, and "1 of 3 done"         |
| `ChatShimmer`                         | `chat`          | "Thinking…" with a shimmer                                     |
| `ChatResponse`                        | `chat-response` | The model's Markdown, completed while it streams; raw HTML never renders |
| `ChatCodeBlock`                       | `chat-response` | Highlighted code with Wrap and Copy (`ChatResponse` uses it for fenced code) |
| `ChatReasoning`                       | `chat-parts`    | The model's thinking: open while it streams, then "Thought for 4s" |
| `ChatTool`                            | `chat-parts`    | A tool call: its status in words, input, output or error       |
| `ChatSources`, `ChatCitation`         | `chat-parts`    | "Used 2 sources", and a numbered link with a hover card        |
| `ChatImage`                           | `chat-parts`    | An image with its size reserved and an optional caption        |
| `ChatComposer`                        | `chat-composer` | The message box: Enter sends, commands, mentions, attachments, a toolbar |
| `ChatModelPicker`, `ChatUsage`        | `chat-composer` | A model `Select`, and a meter that reads "18.4K of 200K tokens" |
| `ChatThreadList`                      | `chat-sidebar`  | The chats: choose one, New chat, Rename, Delete (asks first)   |
| `ChatLauncher`                        | `chat-sidebar`  | A floating button that opens the assistant in a panel          |

## Use

```tsx
<ChatThread label="Conversation">
  {turns.length === 0 && (
    <ChatEmpty title="What are we working on?">
      <ChatSuggestions suggestions={["Draft release notes"]} onSelect={send} />
    </ChatEmpty>
  )}
  {turns.map((turn) =>
    turn.from === "user" ? (
      <ChatMessage key={turn.id} from="user">{turn.text}</ChatMessage>
    ) : (
      <ChatMessage
        key={turn.id}
        from="assistant"
        avatar={{ fallback: "AI" }}
        streaming={turn.streaming}
        actions={!turn.streaming && (
          <ChatMessageActions text={turn.text} onRetry={() => retry(turn.id)}
            feedback={turn.feedback} onFeedbackChange={(f) => rate(turn.id, f)} />
        )}
      >
        {turn.reasoning && (
          <ChatReasoning streaming={turn.thinking} seconds={turn.seconds}>
            {turn.reasoning}
          </ChatReasoning>
        )}
        {turn.tools.map((tool) => (
          <ChatTool key={tool.id} name={tool.name} status={tool.status}
            input={tool.input} output={tool.output} />
        ))}
        <ChatResponse streaming={turn.streaming}>{turn.text}</ChatResponse>
        <ChatSources sources={turn.sources} />
      </ChatMessage>
    ),
  )}
</ChatThread>
<ChatComposer
  running={running}
  onStop={stop}
  onSubmit={({ text, files }) => send(text, files)}
  commands={[{ value: "summarize", label: "summarize", description: "Shorten the thread" }]}
  mentions={projectFiles.map((f) => ({ value: f.path, label: f.name }))}
  attachments={{ accept: "image/*,.pdf", maxFiles: 5, maxSize: 10 * 1024 * 1024 }}
  tools={
    <>
      <ChatModelPicker models={models} value={model} onValueChange={setModel} />
      <ChatUsage used={used} limit={200000} />
    </>
  }
/>
```

- `ChatThread`'s `label` ("Conversation") names its scroll region, which holds a
  `role="log"`. The region is capped at `--chat-thread-height` (26rem by default).
- `ChatMessage` takes `from` (`"user"`, `"assistant"` or `"system"`), `name` (You,
  Assistant or System by default), `avatar` (`{ src?, fallback }`, named by `name`) and
  `time` (a `Date`, shown in the viewer's short time format). `streaming` marks it
  `aria-busy` and draws a caret after the last block.
- `ChatMessageActions` shows Copy when `text` is given, Retry with `onRetry`, Edit with
  `onEdit`, and Good and Bad with `onFeedbackChange`. Pressing the pressed one again gives
  `null`. Copy announces "Copied". `label` names the toolbar ("Message actions").
- `ChatBranch` takes `index` (from 0), `count` and `onIndexChange`, and renders nothing for
  fewer than two versions. "2 of 3" is announced as it changes.
- `ChatTasks` takes `tasks` (`{ id, title, status, detail? }`), `title` ("Plan") and
  `defaultOpen` (on). Statuses `pending`, `running`, `done` and `failed` read as To do,
  In progress, Done and Failed.

## Answers

- `ChatResponse` takes the Markdown as its child, with GitHub tables, task lists and
  strikethrough. With `streaming`, half-written Markdown is completed (remend), so
  `**bold` shows as bold, not stars.
- Raw HTML in the Markdown is dropped, never rendered: model output is untrusted. `http`
  and `https` links open in a new tab and say so to screen readers. Wide tables scroll in
  a focusable region.
- Images in an answer load when they're same-origin, `data:` or `blob:`. Any other image
  shows as a link ("Image: chart"), because its address could carry what the model read
  to another server. `allowImage(url)` returns `true` for the ones to load.
- Fenced code with a language is highlighted by shiki, loaded the first time it's needed,
  one language at a time, in the skin's colors. A language shiki doesn't know shows as
  plain text. Each block has a Wrap toggle and a Copy button named "Copy ts". Render
  `ChatCodeBlock` yourself with `code`, `language` and `filename` (which then names the
  block and its Copy button).
- `ChatReasoning` opens while `streaming` is on and closes when it ends, unless a person
  or an agent opened or closed it; then it stays as they left it. It reads "Thinking…"
  while streaming, "Thought for 4s" with `seconds` (rounded, at least 1), and
  "Reasoning" without.
- `ChatTool`'s `status` is `pending`, `running`, `approval`, `done`, `error` or `denied`,
  read as Queued, Running, Needs your approval, Done, Failed and Not allowed. It opens
  itself for `approval` and `error` unless you pass `defaultOpen`. `title` replaces
  `name` in the header; `input` and `output` show as JSON (strings as they are); `error`
  shows in place of the output.
- `ChatTool` has no Allow or Deny buttons of its own. Put yours in its `children`, which
  render in the panel, and give Allow a `data-agent-confirm` (the web element does).
- `ChatSources` takes `sources` (`{ href, title, description? }`) and renders nothing for
  an empty list. `ChatCitation` takes `index` and one `source`: a link named "Source 1:
  title" whose hover card shows the title, host and description.
- `ChatImage` needs `src`, `alt`, `width` and `height`, so the space is held before it
  loads; `caption` is optional.

## The composer

- `onSubmit({ text, files })` gets the trimmed text and the attached files, then the box
  clears. With no text and no files, nothing is sent.
- While `running` is on, Enter and Send don't send. With `onStop` too, Send becomes Stop.
- `commands` show after "/" at the start of the message and `mentions` after "@", each
  `{ value, label, description? }`. Choosing one inserts the trigger and the label
  ("/summarize "); `onSubmit` gets that text, not the item's `value`.
- `attachments` is off by default. `{ accept?, maxFiles?, maxSize? }` (`maxSize` in bytes)
  adds a paperclip, takes files dropped on the box or pasted into it, and lists them as
  chips with Remove. UI SDK's `FileInput` announces files it rejects; they never join.
- `tools` render in the composer's toolbar, beside Send. `label` ("Message") names the
  box; `placeholder` defaults to "Message…".
- Up brings back messages sent from this box since it mounted.
- `ChatModelPicker` takes `models` (`{ value, label, description? }`), `value` or
  `defaultValue` (the first model when neither is given), `onValueChange` and `label`
  ("Model", visually hidden).
- `ChatUsage` takes `used` and `limit`, with `unit` ("tokens") and `label` ("Context
  used"). The meter carries `data-level="medium"` past 70% and `"high"` past 90%.

## Chats and the launcher

- `ChatThreadList` takes `threads` (`{ id, title, updatedAt? }`), `value` (the open chat,
  marked `aria-current="page"`) and `onValueChange(id)`. `label` names the list ("Chats").
- `onNew` adds New chat. `onRename(id, title)` and `onDelete(id)` add a "More for
  title" menu to each chat. Rename edits in place: Enter or leaving the field saves,
  Escape cancels, and an empty or unchanged title isn't sent. Delete asks in an alert
  dialog ("Delete “Launch plan”?") before calling `onDelete`.
- `updatedAt` shows as "4 min ago" and is the chat button's description. It's worked out
  when the list renders, not kept current.
- `ChatLauncher` takes `label` ("Open assistant"), `title` ("Assistant") and the panel's
  `children`. The panel opens above its button and stays open while you click around
  the page; Escape, the button and Close shut it.

## The chat-app template

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add superzero11/uiset/chat-app
```

`<ChatAppTemplate assistant={assistant} />` is the kit as a page. `assistant` is an async
generator given `{ text, files, model, history, signal }` that yields `text`, `reasoning`,
`reasoning-end`, `tool` (the same `id` updates the card) and `sources` events; the sample
one streams a placeholder. It also takes `models`, `commands`, `mentions`, `suggestions`,
`userName` ("You"), `userAvatar` and `limit` (200000, for the usage meter).

- It runs one answer at a time. Stop aborts `signal` and isn't shown as a failure; any
  other error adds "The answer stopped early. Try again."
- It starts on the second entry in `models` (the sample's "Balanced").
- New chats are numbered ("Untitled chat 2") until the first message, cut to 40
  characters, becomes the title. Deleting the last chat starts a new one.
- Retry sends the question before that answer again, as a new turn.
- Usage is an estimate per chat (`estimateTokens`: 900 plus 4 per character of each
  message sent), until your model reports its own.

[Templates](./templates.md#connecting-a-model-to-chat-app) shows a model connected.

## Keys

| Keys                    | Where                      | Does                                                   |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Enter                   | message box                | Send; with a "/" or "@" menu open, choose the item     |
| Shift+Enter             | message box                | A new line                                             |
| Up, Down                | message box                | What you sent before, when the caret is on the first or last line |
| "/" at the start, "@"   | message box                | Commands, mentions: arrows move, Enter or Tab choose, Escape closes |
| Tab                     | thread, code, tables       | One stop each; arrows and Page keys scroll it          |
| Arrows                  | message actions, suggestions | Move along the toolbar (one Tab stop)               |
| Enter, Space            | reasoning, tool, sources, plan | Open or close it                                   |
| Enter, Escape           | rename field               | Save, cancel (leaving the field saves too)             |
| Escape                  | launcher                   | Close it                                               |

Enter doesn't send while an input method is composing. Copying, version changes and
attached or rejected files are announced.

## For agents

The bridge sees UI SDK components, so messages themselves aren't in its snapshot: give
your agent the conversation from your own state. What it does see, by name:

- **Message box:** a trigger menu named by `label` ("Message") with `insert`, plus Send
  (or Stop) and "Attach files" (`setValue`, `addFiles`, `removeFile`, `clear`, `open`).
  `insert` writes only while the box has focus; without focus it reports success and
  writes nothing. There's no `setValue` on the box.
- **Toolbar:** "Model" is a select an agent sets by a model's label or value; "Context
  used" is a meter it reads (`value`, `min`, `max`).
- **Answers:** each reasoning, tool call, sources list and plan is a collapsible named by
  its header ("Thought for 4s", "Searched the docs, Done", "Used 2 sources"), with
  `setOpen`. "Message actions" is a toolbar to `press` Copy message, Retry message, Edit
  message, Good response or Bad response; "Feedback on this response" also takes
  `setValue`. Code blocks have "Wrap lines" and "Copy ts"; citations are hover cards
  ("Source 1: AbortController").
- **Chats:** New chat, each chat as a button named by its title, and "More for title" to
  `press` Rename or Delete. Rename shows a "Rename title" field; an agent's `setValue`
  fills it, but it's saved only on Enter or when focus leaves it.
- **Delete chat** in the dialog carries `data-agent-confirm` ("Deletes the chat
  “Launch plan” and its messages"), so a step on it waits for the person, or fails with
  "Needs a person" when the bridge has no `allow`.

Names repeat from one answer to the next ("Message actions", "Wrap lines", "Previous
version"). With two answers on the page, a step that names one fails and lists the refs;
retry with a ref, or give each `ChatMessageActions` its own `label`. Nothing in the kit is
`data-agent-hidden`.

## Web Components

`<uiset-chat>`, `<uiset-chat-composer>`, `<uiset-chat-threads>`,
`<uiset-chat-model-picker>` and `<uiset-chat-usage>` are the kit as custom elements.
`<uiset-chat>` draws a whole conversation from AI SDK's `messages` shape, with Allow and
Deny on tool calls that wait for approval. The launcher has no element. See
[Web Components](./web-components.md#chat).


<!-- docs/data-grid.md -->

# Data Grid

A grid for real data, built on UI SDK: thousands of rows, spreadsheet keys, editing in
place, and actions an agent can call. One item, `data-grid`, gives you `DataGrid`,
`DataGridToolbar` and the framework-free pieces under them.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add superzero11/uiset/data-grid
```

## Why it's built this way

UI SDK ships the hard behaviors a grid needs, and the grid is those behaviors wired
together, not a rewrite of them:

| Need                                         | UI SDK piece                       |
| -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| One tab stop, arrows, Home/End, Page keys    | `createGridFocus`                  |
| Select a block, rows or columns; copy it     | `createCellRange`, `textToCells`   |
| Edit in place: Enter, F2, typing, Escape     | `createInlineEdit`                 |
| Render 10,000 rows, reveal one off screen    | `createVirtualizer`                |
| Column menu, View menu, filters, grouping    | `Menu`, `Popover`, `Select`        |
| Drag a column edge                           | `bindDrag`                         |
| Announce sorts, counts and edits             | `announce`                         |
| Agents sort, filter, select and edit         | the primitive's `agent` key        |

Sorting, filtering, grouping and CSV export are plain functions in `data-grid/view.ts`,
so they run on a server or in a worker too.

## Use

```tsx
import { DataGrid, DataGridToolbar, type DataGridColumn } from "@/components/ui/data-grid"

const columns: DataGridColumn<Order>[] = [
  { id: "id", header: "Order", value: (o) => o.id, pinned: true, hideable: false },
  { id: "customer", header: "Customer", value: (o) => o.customer, editable: true },
  { id: "status", header: "Status", value: (o) => o.status, options: ["Paid", "Pending"], editable: true },
  {
    id: "amount",
    header: "Amount",
    type: "number",
    value: (o) => o.amount,
    text: (o) => money.format(o.amount),
    editable: true,
  },
  { id: "rush", header: "Rush", type: "boolean", value: (o) => o.rush, editable: true },
]

<DataGrid
  label="Orders"
  rows={orders}
  columns={columns}
  getRowId={(o) => o.id}
  selectable
  onCellEdit={({ rowId, column, value }) => save(rowId, column, value)}
  persist="orders-grid"
  height="30rem"
>
  <DataGridToolbar filename="orders" selectionActions={<Button>Mark paid</Button>} />
</DataGrid>
```

- `value` is what sorts and filters; `text` is what shows and copies; `render` replaces
  what shows (a badge, a link) without changing either.
- `type` sets how an edit is read, with UI SDK's `parseNumber` and `parseDate` in
  `locale`: `"number"` follows the locale's grouping and accepts a currency sign
  (`$1,200.50`) but refuses words (`12 units`); `"date"` reads "Nov 20", "2026-11-20" or
  the locale's order and stores that calendar day; `"boolean"` flips with Space.
  `options` limits an edit to a list and suggests it.
- `onCellEdit` gets the parsed value. Return `false` to keep the editor open. Without
  it, nothing is editable.
- `sort`, `query`, `filters`, `groupBy`, `selected`, `columnState` and `density` can
  each be controlled (keep filters in the URL, say), with a `default…` and an
  `on…Change`.
- Pass `locale` when rendering on a server, so counts format the same on both sides.
- `persist` saves column order, widths, visibility, pinning and density in
  `localStorage`, read after the first render so server markup matches.

## Toolbar parts

`DataGridToolbar` is one arrangement of parts you can use on their own, anywhere inside
a `DataGrid`: `DataGridSearch`, `DataGridFilters`, `DataGridGroupBy`, `DataGridViewMenu`,
`DataGridExport` and `DataGridSelection` (the count, your bulk actions, Clear selection).
`useDataGrid()` gives a custom part the same state.

```tsx
<DataGrid label="Orders" rows={orders} columns={columns} getRowId={(o) => o.id} selectable>
  <div className="my-toolbar">
    <DataGridSearch />
    <DataGridSelection>
      <Button>Mark paid</Button>
    </DataGridSelection>
    <DataGridExport filename="orders" />
  </div>
</DataGrid>
```

## Keys

| Keys                           | Where         | Does                                         |
| ------------------------------ | ------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Arrows, Home, End, Page keys   | anywhere      | Move one cell, to the row's ends, by a page  |
| Control+Home, Control+End      | anywhere      | First cell, last cell (rows render on the way) |
| Enter, Space                   | header        | Sort ascending, descending, off              |
| Shift+Enter                    | header        | Add the column to the sort                   |
| Shift+F10 or the Menu key      | header        | Column menu: sort, group, pin, move, hide    |
| Alt+Left, Alt+Right            | header        | Narrower, wider (Option on a Mac)            |
| Alt+Shift+Left, Alt+Shift+Right | header       | Move the column                              |
| Enter, F2, or start typing     | editable cell | Edit; Enter saves, Escape cancels, Tab saves |
| Space                          | yes/no cell   | Flip it                                      |
| Space                          | first column  | Check the row                                |
| Enter                          | group row     | Open or close the group                      |
| Shift+Arrows, Shift+click      | anywhere      | Select a block                               |
| Shift+Space, Control+Space     | anywhere      | Select the rows, the columns                 |
| Control+A, Escape              | anywhere      | Select all cells, clear the block            |
| Control+C, Control+V           | anywhere      | Copy the block; paste into editable cells    |

The grid's description lists these for screen reader users, and every sort, resize,
move, paste and filter result is announced. Each header also has a column menu button
for pointers, touch and touch screen readers (it never takes the tab stop), and the menu
has **Wider** and **Narrower**, so resizing never needs a drag.

## For agents

The grid offers `sortBy`, `filter`, `filterColumn`, `selectRows`, `clearSelection`,
`editCell`, `groupBy` and `showColumn`. Columns are named by header and rows by their id
or first column, the way a person reads them. The snapshot shows what the grid is doing
(rows shown, sort, filter, grouping, selection), and `query` returns every row, including
the ones not rendered.

A step that can't run says why, so the agent can try again:

```txt
No column "Total" in Orders. Its columns: Order, Customer, Region, Status, Amount, Placed, Rush.
Amount needs a number
Status must be one of Paid, Pending, Refunded, Failed
```

Edits go through the same parsing and `onCellEdit` as a person's, so your validation
applies to both.

## Accessibility notes

- `role="grid"` with `aria-rowcount` and `aria-rowindex`, so screen readers know the
  full size while only visible rows render.
- The primary sort column carries `aria-sort`. Group cells carry `aria-expanded` (a grid
  row may not; only a treegrid's can).
- Row checkboxes are real checkboxes that never take focus; the cell keeps it, so the
  arrows keep working after a click. Shift-click ranges follow the rows on screen.
- The editor covers its cell, says what's wrong with `aria-invalid` and a message, and
  announces it.
- Range outlines follow the reading direction, and the focused cell's ring is an outline,
  so both hold in right-to-left and in forced colors.

## Limits, for now

- Rows have one height per density; wrapping text is cut with an ellipsis.
- Columns aren't virtualized; hundreds of columns will be slow.
- Find in page only finds rendered rows; use the search box. `createVirtualizer`'s
  `findable` can lift this later.


<!-- docs/charts.md -->

# Charts: design plan

Step 4 of the owner's plan. UI SDK ships no charts, and a dashboard is the first thing
most apps build, so this is a gap a UI SDK developer hits on day one.

## The set (complete-set rule)

What a developer needs to ship dashboards and reports end to end:

| Item            | What it is                                                                  |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `chart`         | The frame every chart shares: title, description, legend, Chart/Table switch, tooltip, scales, palette tokens per skin |
| `line-chart`    | Trend over time; one or more series; area wash for one series; stacked areas |
| `bar-chart`     | Compare categories; vertical or horizontal; grouped or stacked; ranked       |
| `scatter-chart` | Two measures per item; up to three series; nearest-point hover               |
| `heatmap`       | Magnitude on a grid (weekday × hour, day calendar); one hue, scale legend    |
| `segmented-bar` | One whole split into parts, tall (with values) or thin (beside figures)      |
| `sparkline`     | A trend inside text, a table cell or a stat                                  |
| Stat with trend | The existing `stat` gains `delta` direction and a `trend` sparkline          |

No pie or donut. Part-to-whole is a segmented bar (at a glance) or ranked bars (to
compare); the docs say why, so nobody thinks it was forgotten.

## Principles (from the dataviz method, applied to UISet)

- **Form before color.** Every chart's docs start with the job it does.
- **One axis.** No dual-axis option, ever. Two measures → two charts.
- **Color follows the entity.** Series get slots by their place in `series`, so
  isolating or hiding one never repaints the others. There are eight slots; a ninth
  series and beyond draw in the "Other" gray, so fold your tail into one "Other" series.
- **Thin marks.** Bars ≤ 24px with a 4px rounded data end, square at the baseline; 2px
  lines with round joins; markers ≥ 8px with a 2px surface ring; area wash ~10%;
  hairline solid grid and axes, never dashed; 2px surface gap between touching fills.
- **Labels in ink, never series color.** Identity rides a swatch or line key beside it.
  Direct labels only at line ends (≤ 4 series) and bar tips where they fit.
- **Legend for two or more series**, and it doubles as a filter: pressing a legend
  entry isolates or hides a series (toggle buttons, `aria-pressed`).
- **Every chart has a table twin.** A Chart/Table switch shows the same data as a real
  `<table>`. Tooltips enhance; they never gate.
- **Hover and focus show the same thing.** Line/area: a crosshair snaps to the nearest
  x and the tooltip lists every series there. Bars, cells, dots: the mark is the
  target, at least 24px, and lifts on hover.

## Keyboard and screen readers

The SVG is drawing only (`aria-hidden`). Over it sits an HTML layer of hit targets, one
per data position (an x for lines, a bar, a cell, a point), which is what people and
assistive tech use:

- The layer is a `listbox` with one tab stop, from UI SDK's roving focus with a custom
  `move`: arrows follow the chart's direction (`aria-orientation` says which), and in a
  heatmap Up and Down move a row and stop at the edges. Home and End jump. Charts draw
  left to right in every language, so Right is always the next position.
- Each target is an `option` whose name is the full reading: "March 3: Revenue $12,400,
  Costs $8,100". Selecting one pins it (and is a cross-filter hook: `onSelect`).
- Moving announces nothing extra: the option's name is the announcement.
- Targets are the hit areas for the pointer too, so hover and focus share one code path
  and the hit area is the whole band, never a 2px line.

## For agents

Each chart is a UI SDK primitive with an `agent` key: `items` returns the data as rows,
so `query` can answer "what was revenue in March?" without a screenshot, and actions
`isolate`, `showAll`, `showTable` and `select` let an agent drive the view. `select` takes
what people read ("March") before a key. The Chart/Table switch is hidden from agents while
the chart shows, since `showTable` does its job; with the table showing, the chart's actions
are out of reach, so the switch is open to agents as the way back.

## Color per skin (validated, not eyeballed)

Tokens: `--chart-1` … `--chart-8` (categorical), `--chart-seq-1` … `-7` (sequential, one
hue), `--chart-neg`/`--chart-mid`/`--chart-pos` (diverging), plus grid, axis and ink.
Each skin sets them; base.css draws with them.

| Skin, scheme         | Surface   | Palette                                              | Result |
| -------------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| Base, light          | `#fdfdff` | reference light set                                  | all gates pass; aqua, yellow, magenta < 3:1 → relief: direct labels + table view |
| Base, dark           | `#0e0f13` | reference dark set                                   | all gates pass, all ≥ 3:1 |
| Studio (dark only)   | `#34383e` | reference dark set                                   | all gates pass; magenta, green < 3:1 → same relief |
| Blueprint (dark only) | `#053d75` | `#9da3ef #73edb1 #fd8537 #f55fad #fed917 #ffc4fe #b2e37e #73c3ff` | adjacent CVD 14.6, normal 18.7; first six all-pairs CVD 9.3, normal 17.3; all ≥ 3:1 |

The gates are the validator's: adjacent pairs, which is what bars and lines need. Pairs
that aren't neighbors can still be close in the reference sets (light pink and orange,
dark green and pink under deutan vision), so charts never lean on color alone: a scatter
chart's series differ in shape, a segmented bar labels its parts, and every chart has its
table. Blueprint's first six clear every pair as well, since its mid-blue paper leaves
less room between colors. `tests/unit/chart-palette.test.ts` measures them, so a re-picked
color that brings back a lookalike pair fails.

Blueprint's set sits above the validator's dark lightness band (0.48–0.67) on purpose:
the band assumes a near-black surface, and on mid-blue paper (L 0.36) colors inside it
fall under 3:1. Contrast is the check the band stands in for, and it passes.

## Look

Charts take the skin. Base: quiet hairlines and the palette. Blueprint: the skin's
white linework for axes, grid and crosshair, and its light colored-pencil set. Studio: the
amber lamp as the crosshair and the sequential ramp.

## Use

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add superzero11/uiset/line-chart superzero11/uiset/bar-chart \
  superzero11/uiset/scatter-chart superzero11/uiset/heatmap \
  superzero11/uiset/segmented-bar superzero11/uiset/sparkline
```

Every chart takes `title` (its name for people and agents), `data`, and accessors.
`format` formats values in tooltips, labels and the table.

```tsx
<LineChart
  title="Revenue and costs"
  description="2026, by month"
  data={months}
  x={(d) => d.month}
  series={[
    { key: "revenue", label: "Revenue", value: (d) => d.revenue },
    { key: "costs", label: "Costs", value: (d) => d.costs },
  ]}
  format={(n) => money.format(n)}
/>

<BarChart title="Revenue by region" data={regions} x={(d) => d.region}
  series={[{ key: "revenue", label: "Revenue", value: (d) => d.revenue }]}
  orientation="horizontal" sort="descending" />

<SegmentedBar title="Traffic sources" parts={[{ key: "search", label: "Search", value: 189000 }, …]} />

<Heatmap title="Sessions by day and hour" data={sessions} rows={days} columns={hours}
  row={(d) => d.day} column={(d) => d.hour} value={(d) => d.sessions} measure="Sessions" />

<ScatterChart title="Deal size and time to close" data={deals} label={(d) => d.name}
  x={(d) => d.days} y={(d) => d.size} xLabel="Days to close" yLabel="Deal size" />

<Stat label="Revenue" value="$91,000" change={{ value: "9.6%", direction: "up" }}
  trend={lastTwelveMonths} />
```

`Sparkline` and `Stat` hold no state, so they render in a Server Component.

```tsx
<LineChart title="Visits by channel" layout="stacked" data={…} x={…} series={…} />
```

- `LineChart`: `layout` is `"line"`, `"area"` (a wash under each line) or `"stacked"`
  (areas to a total, whose readings and table include the total); `zero` keeps zero on
  the axis (default on). Stacks with negative layers stay inside the plot.
- `BarChart`: `orientation` (`"vertical"` columns or `"horizontal"` bars), `layout`
  (`"grouped"` or `"stacked"`), `sort`, `labels`.
- `ScatterChart`: `series` takes up to three groups, each with a `match`.
- `SegmentedBar`: `variant="thin"` for an 8px bar beside its figures.
- `selected` / `onSelect` pin a data position from outside, for cross-filtering a
  dashboard: select a month in one chart, filter the others. Keys are the datum's index
  in `data`, however a bar chart sorts it. `onSelect(key, { source, reason })` says who
  pinned it (`keyboard`, `pointer`, `agent`) and why; when new data drops the pinned
  position, it fires once with `null` and `{ source: "data", reason: "removed" }`. A
  controlled `selected` that the page doesn't change refuses the pin.
- `locale` formats axis ticks, readings and shares; pass it when rendering on a server
  so the server and the browser print the same digits.
- `ChartFrame` is exported for charts of your own: compute the drawing and the data
  positions, and it supplies the rest.

## Keys

| Keys                    | Does                                               |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Tab                     | Into the chart (one stop) and out again            |
| Left, Right (Up, Down)  | The next data position; bar charts on their side use Up and Down |
| Up, Down in a heatmap   | The cell above or below                            |
| Home, End               | The first or last position                         |
